note: The tools the chats call through the harness core (services.py). The descriptions are short on purpose: when to use each one, and what not to do, is in SKILL.md.

tools.name: mas_create_task
tools.description: Create a task from the owner's request. Nothing runs yet: you get the route the written rule picked, with the reasoning, and an intent_id for the ONE chat question in which the owner approves that exact route (relay HIS answer with mas_answer), and the task then runs and is checked by code. You never give the task's level: the harness derives it from the owner's profile and what the text touches (touches), and asks the owner when it cannot tell. The first time it also asks him a few profile questions: relay them, never answer them. The text is the owner's, whole: if it is long, do not shorten it; the result says how many characters arrived. For work no catalog task type names, the result is a recommendation and ONE question for the owner (relay it, never answer it); the task is created only after his answer. To work on the contents of a folder of one of his computers, pass it in inputs; the harness asks him, reads it, finds or proposes a local model if none is ready, and resumes the task by itself.

text.description: the task input, as the owner gave it (the text to summarize, the code to fix...)

task_type.description: the kind of work. A catalog task type when one fits (see the list below); otherwise a short plain description of the kind of work (for example `contract review`, at most 40 characters, never the task text). A description no catalog type names does not fail: the harness recommends an environment from what it knows and asks the owner one question.

check.description: an optional check graded by code: {kind: equals|contains|regex|sha256, value} or {kind: project_tests, files: {path: text}, pattern}. Without one the result is shown but not graded.

touches.description: which of the owner's categories the text concerns (the values come from his profile), "none" if it concerns none of them, "unsure" if you cannot tell. This is a statement about the text, not a level.

domain.description: optional free tags for the field the work belongs to (for example `legal`, `finance`, `grant writing`); short plain words, never the task text. An environment tagged for it is preferred.

inputs.description: optional things the HARNESS reads from one of the owner's computers for this task, after he approves each one (for example {kind: folder, machine: the computer's name, folder: Desktop}). You never see what is read: only the model's answer comes back to you. Use this instead of asking for the folder's contents.

tools.name: mas_explain_route
tools.description: Explain which route a task takes and why, right now: the candidates, each environment that was left out with its reason, what each filter cut, and what the written rule chose. Give a task_id, or a task_type and sensitivity. It changes nothing.

tools.name: mas_run_admission
tools.description: Measure one environment on a task type's 10-task suite (graded by code, pass mark 8/10). It spends the owner's machine time, so you get an intent_id and the owner answers ONE chat question (relay HIS answer with mas_answer). Name the environment and the task type; add machine or access if more than one combination fits.

tools.name: mas_job
tools.description: What happened to a task, an admission exam or an access change: its state, each attempt and its code check, the result (withheld from a cloud chat when it is confidential) and the step waiting for the owner. Call it again only when something may have changed (after the owner answered), not in a row.

job_id.description: the task id, admission id or job id a tool gave you

tools.name: mas_add_access
tools.description: Connect a computer to an API, provider or account: add an access (an API key) on one machine, from the accesses the catalog lists (the access argument is one of them). The owner types the key into a hidden window of the operating system; you never see it, never ask for it and never accept it in the chat. You get a job_id; the owner's approval dialog and then the key window open on his screen by themselves. Follow with mas_job.

access.description: the access id, for example meta-model-api:api-key

variable.description: only when the access accepts more than one variable name

tools.name: mas_remove_access
tools.description: Remove an access from one machine: its key is set aside in that machine's credential store (not deleted, never shown). It goes through a plan and the owner's system dialog. With undo set to true it brings the key back.

tools.name: mas_board_start
tools.description: Start a board for a goal that needs several steps (for example 'build a small CLI with tests'). A director breaks it into subtasks, the router routes each one, results are checked by code and verified on another machine. You then show the plan and the owner approves it once. A cloud chat cannot start a confidential board.

sensitivity.description: ask the owner if he has not said; never guess

tools.name: mas_board_show
tools.description: Show a board: its subtasks, where each one runs and how it is checked, and what waits for the owner (the plan to approve, an escalation to confirm). Call it until the board has stopped or something waits for him.

tools.name: mas_board_approve
tools.description: Ask the owner to approve one pending decision of a board (the plan, or an escalation beyond what he allowed). You get an intent_id; the owner answers ONE chat question (relay HIS answer with mas_answer). You cannot approve for him.

tools.name: mas_measurements
tools.description: What has been measured for a task type: every combination's admission result (pass rate, median time, still fresh or not), the candidates with no measurement (listed, never ranked), and the recommendation, which comes from measured numbers only. Use it to compare models or environments the owner has had measured.

tools.name: mas_draft
tools.description: The draft of the whole network's setup: action 'start' makes the agent propose it from what it sees; 'correct' (with the owner's own words in text) makes it draft again from his correction; 'approve' asks him to approve the proposed draft in his own system dialog. Follow a draft run with mas_status and answer its questions with mas_answer.

text.description: only for correct: the owner's words, as he said them

tools.name: mas_profile
tools.description: The owner's profile: what is confidential for him, his stance on cloud spend, local-first, what each machine is for, and what he closed. show reads it (and the next question if answers are missing); ask puts the next question; set, role, close and open change it with HIS words. Closing something is a question to him; open undoes it. Never fill an answer in yourself. clear asks him whether a subscription tool he has (named in id) may be used automatically; unclear takes that back.

tools.name: mas_propose
tools.description: What the owner's machines can do now (which environments for which task types, from what is detected) and what each other one needs first, built by the harness from the catalog, as one proposal with one question for the owner. Present it as it is; do not add options of your own.

tools.name: mas_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a run that is still open (for example one waiting for an answer the owner never wants to give). run_id is the one a tool printed. What the run already did stays; mas_undo takes back a finished setup.

tools.name: mas_install_tool
tools.description: Install a command-line tool from the catalog (for example a coding harness) on a paired computer, or remove it again (action undo). The harness builds the plan from the catalog's pinned files (address, size, SHA-256 per system) and the computer's analysis; you get an intent_id and the owner answers ONE chat question showing the whole plan (relay HIS answer with mas_answer). An entry whose install data is not verified is refused with its reason (no_installer or unverified_entry). The computer must have a stored analysis.

tools.name: mas_refresh_models
tools.description: Read the models an API environment lists now (for example the Meta API), through the paired computer that holds its key: no key passes through the coordinator or the chat. The harness keeps the dated list and says which chat models the router may then offer for that environment. The result arrives as a job (mas_job).

tools.name: mas_measure_recommender
tools.description: Measure the recommender with the cloud model (the Meta API), reached through the paired computer that holds its key: the 12 fixed gold tasks and the 6 fixed domains, with and without the harness, bounded by a call cap. You get an intent_id and the owner answers ONE chat question showing what will be spent (relay HIS answer with mas_answer). It needs his recorded answer on cloud use. The numbers arrive as a job (mas_job).
